speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) what is the assessment of recent reported incidents of knife crime incidents where individuals use knives to harm others; (b) whether there has been an up-trend and, if so, what are the assessed reasons; and (c) what is being done to ensure that Singaporeans continue to have a safe and secure living environment.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs in light of the recent knife attack at a place of worship, what is being done beyond higher frequency in Police patrols to provide personal safety assurance at places of worship.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: I believe these are in relation to Dr Tan's questions, and as well as a subsequent question filed by Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim1 which is scheduled for a subsequent Sitting.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: I also invite Mr Zhulkarnain to seek clarifications if needed and if the questions are satisfactorily answered today, it may not be necessary for Mr Zhulkarnain to proceed with his question subsequently.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sorry, Minister of State Sun, this will also cover Question No 53 in today's Order Paper, filed by Mr Christopher de Souza?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) does not track the cases by whether the offenders had mental health issues.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Our Police officers are trained and equipped to deal with crimes involving knives and will respond swiftly to neutralise the threat when alerted.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: When there is information on specific threats or when the general threat level is escalated, the Police will step up security measures, such as increasing the frequency of patrols.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: They will also engage with relevant stakeholders to ensure that appropriate security measures are put in place.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: To safeguard public safety, we also limit the sale of certain types of knives and similar offensive weapons, which have limited legitimate use.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: While the incidence of crimes involving knives is low, it is important, nevertheless, that we all know how to respond when such attacks occur.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The November 2024 incident at St Joseph's Church is a case in point.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We must therefore continue to systematically build up the resilience of our society to emergencies, and we have been doing this over the years.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Police and the Singapore Civil Defence Force work with building owners and managers across Singapore via the Safety and Security Watch Group to conduct security audits, share best practices and deliver training on building safety and security awareness.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Exercises are regularly conducted to test contingency response plans and ground readiness in the event of emergencies.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We also work closely with community and religious organisations, including places of worship, through the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth's Crisis Preparedness for Religious Organisations Programme, where religious organisations participate in security self-assessments, develop contingency plans and attend counter-terrorism seminars to understand the threat better.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Outreach efforts include sharing advisories, such as "Run, Hide, Tell" and "Press, Tie, Tell", as well as the importance of learning emergency preparedness skills, such as first aid, cardiopulmonary resuscitation and the use of automated external defibrillators.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Together, these measures help ensure a high level of public safety, security awareness and contingency readiness in our society.
